title: Count Smaller Values to the Right
statement: For every array element, count how many later elements are strictly smaller than it. Equal values are not counted as smaller. Return one count for each original position, preserving input order. A quadratic scan is too slow for large sequences. A merge-sort counting method can count how many right-half values pass each left-half value while merging; alternatively, coordinate compression with a Fenwick tree can count previously processed values from right to left.

title: Lowest Shared Ancestor in a Tree
statement: A rooted tree is given with vertex 1 as the root. For each query containing two vertices u and v, report their lowest common ancestor: the deepest vertex that is an ancestor of both. The tree edges are undirected, so root it before answering queries. constraints: 1 <= n,q <= 100000; edges form a tree; vertices are 1..n

from collections import deque
d=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()));n,q=d[:2];g=[[] for _ in range(n)];p=2

par=[-1]*n;dep=[0]*n;qq=deque([0]);par[0]=0
while qq:
 u=qq.popleft()
 for v in g[u]:
  if par[v]<0:par[v]=u;dep[v]=dep[u]+1;qq.append(v)
out=[]
for _ in range(q):u,v=d[p]-1,d[p+1]-1;p+=2
 while dep[u]>dep[v]:u=par[u]
 while dep[v]>dep[u]:v=par[v]

print('\n'.join(out))
